chunks: By this chain of narration, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abd al-Aziz, from Ibn Abi Ya'fur, who said: Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) said:

When you pray an obligatory prayer, pray it on time like the prayer of one bidding farewell who fears he will never return to it again. Then direct your gaze toward the place of your prostration, for if you knew who was to your right and to your left, you would have perfected your prayer. And know that you are before Him who sees you while you cannot see Him.

key_terms.سجود: Prostration -- placing the forehead on the ground in prayer, symbolizing ultimate submission to God
key_terms.صلاة فريضة: Obligatory prayer -- one of the five daily prayers required of every Muslim
key_terms.مودع: One bidding farewell -- praying as if it were one's last prayer

ai.seo_question: How should one pray the obligatory prayer according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) instructs his companion Ibn Abi Ya'fur on perfecting obligatory prayer. The teaching was directed at dedicated students of the Imam in Medina during the 2nd century AH. The Imam advises praying each obligatory prayer at its appointed time with the urgency and devotion of a farewell prayer, maintaining focus on the place of prostration, and cultivating awareness of God's presence -- the concept of ihsan (spiritual excellence in worship).

en.bilal-muhammad: By this isnad from al-Hasan b. Mahbub from `Abd al-`Aziz from Ibn Abi Ya`fur. He said: Abu `Abdillah al-Sadiq (as) said:

When you pray an obligatory prayer, then pray it on-time in a meek way, fearing that you will never return to it again. Look to the place of your prostration (humble your sight), for if you knew who was to your right and to your left, you would have perfected your prayer. Know that you are before He who sees you while you cannot see Him.
